key_insight: Agentic Symbolic Search (ASYS) uses prior-guided symbolic program search plus gradient fitting to recover or approximate interpretable PDE laws beyond meshes, neural nets, and hand-crafted formulas.
engineering_relevance: The framework can generate human-readable surrogate equations for complex PDE dynamics, helping engineers and scientists analyze, validate, and reason about systems with limited closed-form understanding.
method: An agent encodes PDE theory, problem constraints, and prior search experience into differentiable symbolic programs.
Evolutionary search refines the mathematical form while gradient-based optimization fits continuous parameters.
The approach acts as inductive-bias injection rather than blind symbolic regression.
evidence_signal: Across five PDE problems spanning bounded dynamics, finite-time blow-up, and free-boundary focusing, the abstract reports interpretable formulas including an Allen-Cahn interface law and a nine-parameter Keller-Segel contraction law.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of priors, search space design, and optimization stability, so results may not transfer uniformly to all PDE classes.
paper_title: Agentic Symbolic Search: Characterizing PDEs Beyond Hand-crafted Expressions, Meshes, and Neural Networks
